note: Questions from the CBSE Class XII English (Core) board exam 2025, Q.P. code 1/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. Answers are model answers and value points written for this portal, not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text:
Read the following passage carefully :
(1) Marketing is all about creativity and expression, so it must be an art, right? Not necessarily. While marketers once relied purely on instinct, they now rely on data-driven insights. On top of that, cutting-edge technologies and analytics have shifted the focus of marketing farther toward the science side of the spectrum. Armed with so much data, marketers can now track the impact of money spent on their bottom line.
(2) In today's world, the best approach to marketing combines both disciplines. And there's a distinct balance to the craft – a strategic mix of interpersonal empathy and tactical analysis. Neither side of the mix can be isolated or ignored, or the results will not be encouraging. Psychologists believe the brain is separated into two distinct functions : the left-brain and the right-brain. The right side of the brain is responsible for creative thinking and artistic intuition.
(3) As an art, marketing is all about understanding the nuances of human behaviour and determining how to make an emotional connection with the customer. More importantly, some level of art is needed to create brand standards for your company, including the logo, messaging, and overall visual identity for a brand.
(4) Right-brained marketers focus on the creative – the copy, graphics and emotions tied to the message. The science side of marketing tells us to let the data guide what strategies will be most effective. Marketers are now reporting the need for digital-first expertise including digital proficiency, data analysis, and data science. With science, marketers adopt an outcome-centric mindset that helps them curate smarter campaigns. Over the past few years, there has been an evolving prioritization on data-savvy talent. In 2020 and beyond, brands will need to focus on recruiting talent that can understand the complexities of AI and machine technologies.
(5) But when we reflect on earlier times, marketing was defined as the predominance of traditional advertising, like television, newspaper, and direct mail. Today, it ropes in digital channels, social media, mobile devices, and integrated, complex campaigns. And just as consumers today are more tech-savvy, employees should be able to match – and exceed – their expertise. It's important that brands continue to prioritize creative, engaging campaign messages while also focusing on key insights and performance metrics for optimal results.

Answer the following questions, based on the passage above :
(i) According to paragraph 1, how does the author describe the evolution of marketing? (2)
(ii) Choose ONE statement that aptly reflects the point of view of the writer : (a) In the field of marketing, there is a conflict between Art and Science. (b) Art and Science should work in tandem to do effective marketing. (1)
(iii) Provide ONE textual evidence with reference to paragraph 3 to support that marketing is an art. (1)
(iv) Based on the passage, assess the way data and digital platforms have transformed the field of marketing and employment. (2)
(v) '______ cutting-edge technologies and analytics have shifted the focus of marketing.' (Para 1) By 'cutting-edge technologies', the writer refers to ______. (1)
(vi) Complete the analogy with ONE word from paragraph 2 — included : incorporated :: ______ : secluded. (A) approach (B) empathy (C) isolated (D) intuition (1)
(vii) 'Marketing is all about understanding the nuances of human behaviour.' (Para 3) The writer uses the word 'nuances' to denote (A) man's appreciation for art (B) man's preference for branded clothes (C) the complexities of human character (D) human inclination for analytical approach (1)
(viii) Complete : According to the writer, modern marketing is built on both ______ and ______. (1)
(ix) '______ exceed their expertise.' (Para 5) With reference to paragraph 5, what skills should employees possess to match the demand of the consumers? (1)
(x) What fascinating fact about the human brain is revealed by the writer in the passage? (1)
questions.solution: (i) Marketing once relied purely on instinct and creativity, but it now relies on data-driven insights; technology and analytics have shifted it towards the science side, so marketers can track the impact of money spent. (ii) (b). (iii) 'Marketing is all about understanding the nuances of human behaviour and determining how to make an emotional connection with the customer' (or: art is needed to create brand standards such as the logo and visual identity). (iv) Marketing has moved from traditional advertising (TV, newspapers, direct mail) to digital channels, social media and data-guided, outcome-centric campaigns; employers now prioritise digital proficiency, data analysis, data science and an understanding of AI. (v) the latest, most advanced technologies such as AI, machine learning and data analytics. (vi) (C) isolated. (vii) (C). (viii) art (creativity / empathy) and science (data / analysis). (ix) Tech-savvy, digital and data-analysis skills, matching and exceeding the consumers' own expertise. (x) The brain has two distinct functions: the right side handles creative thinking and artistic intuition, while the left side handles analysis.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text:
Case Study : Tourism in India
(1) Introduction : India, with its rich cultural heritage, diverse landscapes, and historical sites, attracts millions of tourists each year. Tourism significantly contributes to India's GDP, generating employment and boosting infrastructure. This case study explores factors impacting tourism in India, examines seasonal patterns, and assesses tourist satisfaction through a survey.
(2) Methodology : The study involved primary data collection through a structured survey targeting 500 tourists across major destinations like Delhi, Jaipur, Goa and Kerala. Additionally, secondary data from government reports and tourism boards were used. The survey included questions about preferences, challenges and satisfaction levels, focusing on various demographics, including international and domestic tourists.
(3) Survey Examination : Tourists were surveyed on travel preferences, challenges encountered, accommodation satisfaction and cultural experiences. Feedback highlighted India's appeal due to its history and cultural diversity, but also noted issues like infrastructure gaps and pollution.
(4) Results : The study found that most tourists preferred historical sites and beaches. International tourists were drawn to heritage sites, while domestic tourists preferred nature destinations. Satisfaction was high among tourists who experienced local culture, but infrastructure issues and overcrowding at key locations were common complaints. Overall, 85% of tourists expressed a desire to revisit.

(i) Complete : In the introduction, the researcher links tourism to India's GDP to highlight ______. (1)
(ii) What would 'The study involved primary data collection through a structured survey' be classified as? (A) Primary purpose (B) Secondary objective (C) Method of analysis (D) Research outcome (1)
(iii) Give two points to support why the study involved primary and secondary data. (2)
(iv) Classify as 'preference' or 'challenge' : Sentence 1 – Feedback highlighted India's appeal due to its history and cultural diversity. Sentence 2 – Also noted issues like infrastructure gaps and pollution. (2)
(v) List any two points tourists were asked about in the survey. (1)
(vi) What were the more preferred destinations? (1)
(vii) Analyse why, though there was satisfaction among tourists, there were some complaints. (1)
(viii) What is the ultimate goal for stakeholders, based on the insights from the study? (A) tourists expressed a desire to revisit (B) tourists will visit historical sites (C) domestic tourism will increase (D) to promote India as a tourist destination (1)
questions.solution: (i) the economic importance of tourism: it generates employment and boosts infrastructure. (ii) (C) Method of analysis. (iii) Primary data gave first-hand, current information on tourists' preferences, challenges and satisfaction; secondary data from government reports and tourism boards gave reliable background and broader statistics to support and cross-check the survey. (iv) Sentence 1: preference; Sentence 2: challenge. (v) Any two: travel preferences, challenges encountered, accommodation satisfaction, cultural experiences. (vi) Historical sites and beaches. (vii) Tourists enjoyed India's culture and history, but infrastructure gaps, pollution and overcrowding at key places spoiled part of the experience. (viii) (D).

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: Your school is organising an Education Fair in the school premises. As the Head boy / Head girl of Sunshine Public School, Agra, draft a notice in about 50 words informing students of Classes IX – XII about the fair. Include other necessary details. You are Muskan / Manoj. Put your notice in a box.
questions.solution: Format (1): school name, NOTICE, date, heading, name and designation of writer. Content (2): purpose of the fair (career and higher-education guidance), date, time, venue, institutions and counsellors taking part, who can attend, whom to contact. Expression (1): concise, formal language.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: Your school is organising an inter-house 'Maths Quiz' competition. As president of the Quiz Club, draft a notice in about 50 words informing students of Classes IX – XII about the competition. Include necessary details regarding the number of participants, registration date, etc. You are Akila / Akhil. Put your notice in a box.
questions.solution: Format (1): school name, NOTICE, date, heading, signature with name and designation. Content (2): event, date, time, venue, eligibility, number of participants per house, rounds, last date and place for registration, contact person. Expression (1).

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: You are Mr. Abhishek Sharma. You are planning to celebrate your parents' 50th wedding anniversary in a grand manner. Draft a formal invitation card in about 50 words for your friends and relatives. Mention all necessary details.
questions.solution: Format (1): third-person formal invitation with RSVP. Content (2): occasion (golden jubilee of Mr. and Mrs. Sharma), date, time, venue, programme (dinner etc.), host's name, RSVP contact. Expression (1).

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: You are Mrs. Sonali Gupta, a nutritionist. You are invited by the Principal of Radiant Public School, Jammu to address the students on 'Forming Healthy Food Habits'. Write a formal letter of reply in about 50 words accepting the invitation.
questions.solution: Format (1): sender's address, date, receiver's address, subject, salutation, complimentary close. Content (2): thanks for the invitation, acceptance, confirmation of date, time and topic, any requirements (projector, audience size). Expression (1).

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: You are Radhika / Rakesh of 43, J.N. Colony, Cochin. You read an advertisement by EduNet Innovations, 46 Rose Avenue, Bangalore, for a Marketing Executive (qualifications: graduation in Commerce with post-graduation in Marketing, Advertising, Business or Economics; skills: strong communication, presentation and interpersonal skills, proficiency in software and data analysis, attention to detail; experience: minimum 2 years). Write a job application along with your bio-data in 120-150 words.
questions.solution: Format (1): sender's address, date, addressee (The General Manager), subject, salutation, close; separate bio-data. Content (3): reference to the advertisement, interest in the post, summary of suitability; bio-data with personal details, qualifications (B.Com, MBA/M.A. in Marketing), skills, at least 2 years' experience, references. Expression (1): fluency and accuracy.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: You are Kirti / Keshav of 7, M.G. Road, Jhansi. You observe that students who come on a one-day picnic to public parks leave plastic bottles and cans littered all over the park. You are disturbed by this and write a letter to the editor of a national daily in 120-150 words suggesting ways to inculcate civic sense among students. (Cues: role of parents and school in inculcating civic sense; ways to sensitise students – involve them in community projects, emphasise civic responsibility; demonstrate civic behaviour in daily routine.)
questions.solution: Format (1): sender's address, date, The Editor, newspaper, subject, salutation, close. Content (3): the problem observed, its effects on the environment and public spaces, suggestions: parents and teachers as role models, value education, community and cleanliness drives, clear rules and dustbins, rewards for responsible behaviour. Expression (1).

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: Children today are increasingly dependent on AI to complete school tasks such as writing an article, answering questions and making presentations, so they are unable to discover their own creative potential. However, AI can also be judiciously used for the benefit of children. Write an article in 120-150 words on how Artificial Intelligence can be judiciously used for the benefit of students. You are Nirja of XII A. (Cues: helps in digital literacy; enhances learning by giving real-time feedback; facilitates collaborative learning.)
questions.solution: Format (1): title and writer's name. Content (3): introduction to AI in education; benefits — digital literacy, personalised learning and real-time feedback, collaborative tools, accessibility; cautions against over-dependence, plagiarism and loss of creativity; balanced use under teacher guidance. Expression (1).

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: You are Chayan, student reporter of S.M. Public School, Bhopal. Your school celebrated the annual winter carnival where various stalls, games and shows were put up by students. Write a comprehensive report of the event in 120-150 words to be published in your school magazine. (Organise by Who – What – When – Where – Why – How.)
questions.solution: Format (1): heading, byline, place and date. Content (3): occasion, date, venue, chief guest, stalls (food, games, handicrafts), shows and performances, participation, purpose (fund-raising, team spirit), highlights and conclusion. Expression (1).

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
It would be an exotic moment
without rush, without engines.
we would all be together
in a sudden strangeness
Fishermen in the cold sea
would not harm whales
and the man gathering salt
would look back at his hurt hands. (Keeping Quiet)

(i) How, according to the poet, can we create this exotic moment?
(ii) Choose the correct option : The outcome of the fisherman's activity led to the ______ (destruction / protection) of the environment.
(iii) What is the common outcome of this exotic moment? (A) No rush and no mechanisation (B) Men would be gathering salt (C) There would be a strangeness among warring nations (D) Fisherman will look at his hurt hands
(iv) Choose the correct option : The tone of the poet is ______ (appealing / introspective) in the line 'and the man gathering salt would look back at his hurt hands.'
(v) The poet uses the expression 'sudden strangeness' to suggest ______.
(vi) Assertion : The poet advocates taking a break to introspect on the damage inflicted by man. Reason : Introspection will make man's life better. (A) Both true, but R is not the correct explanation (B) Both true, and R is the correct explanation (C) A true, R false (D) A false, R true
questions.solution: (i) By keeping quiet and still for a moment (counting up to twelve), stopping all activity. (ii) destruction. (iii) (A). (iv) introspective. (v) an unusual feeling of togetherness and peace when everyone stops their hurried activity at the same time. (vi) (B).

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
A thing of beauty is a joy forever
Its loveliness increases, it will never
pass into nothingness; but will keep
A bower quiet for us, and a sleep
Full of sweet dreams, and health, and quiet breathing,
Therefore, on every morrow are we wreathing
A flowery band to bind us to the earth. (A Thing of Beauty)

(i) By the phrase 'joy forever' the poet refers to things (A) that make people extremely happy (B) that are a feast to the eyes (C) that are a constant source of happiness (D) that are beautiful but transient
(ii) Choose the correct option : By 'never pass into nothingness' the poet states that nature's beauty will create a ______ (lasting / temporary) impression on man's mind.
(iii) How does Keats make it evident that there is a link between man's wellness and nature's beauty?
(iv) Assertion : Keats states that man derives strength and inspiration from the beauty of nature. Reason : Nature gives physical, emotional and mental solace to man. (A) Both true, R is the correct explanation (B) Both true, R is not the correct explanation (C) A false, R true (D) A true, R false
(v) Select one phrase from the extract which implies that man wants to continue his life on this earth despite innumerable problems.
(vi) Complete : 'a sleep full of sweet dreams' implies ______.
questions.solution: (i) (C). (ii) lasting. (iii) He says a thing of beauty gives 'a sleep full of sweet dreams, and health, and quiet breathing', i.e. peace of mind and good health. (iv) (A). (v) 'A flowery band to bind us to the earth'. (vi) a peaceful, restful and contented mind, free from worry.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
At midnight when the town slept in peace, the Dewan and his aged wife dragged the tiger to the car and shoved it into the seat. The Dewan himself drove the car straight to the forest where the Maharaja was hunting. When they reached the forest, the tiger launched its Satyagraha and refused to get out of the car. The Dewan was thoroughly exhausted in his efforts to haul the beast out of the car and push it down to the ground.
On the following day, the same old tiger wandered into the Maharaja's presence and stood as if in humble supplication, 'Master, what do you command of me?' It was with boundless joy that the Maharaja took careful aim at the beast. The tiger fell in a crumpled heap. (The Tiger King)

(i) How did the Dewan manage to take the tiger to the forest? (A) He conceded to the tiger's satyagraha (B) He pushed the tiger into the car and drove to the forest (C) He hauled the tiger into the tent (D) He persuaded the tiger into a humble supplication of the Maharaja
(ii) Choose the correct option : The attitude of the Dewan can be described as ______ (negligent and reluctant / meek and servile).
(iii) Select one statement or expression from the extract that reflects the humorous writing style of the author.
(iv) State one reason for the 'boundless joy of the Maharaja'.
questions.solution: (i) (B). (ii) meek and servile. (iii) 'the tiger launched its Satyagraha and refused to get out of the car' (or: 'stood as if in humble supplication, "Master, what do you command of me?"'). (iv) It was his hundredth tiger, completing his vow and, he believed, saving him from the astrologer's prophecy.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.chapter: Vistas: Journey to the End of the Earth
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
The rapid increase of human populations has left us battling with other species for limited resources, and the unmitigated burning of fossil fuels has now created a blanket of carbon dioxide around the world, which is slowly but surely increasing the average global temperature.
Climate change is one of the most hotly contested environmental debates of our time. Will the west Antarctic ice sheet melt entirely? Will the Gulf stream ocean current be disrupted? Will it be the end of the world as we know it? (Journey to the End of the Earth)

(i) List one way in which the increasing human population is affecting other species.
(ii) Choose the option that best reflects the tone of the writer in the last line : (A) happy and excited (B) encouraging and optimistic (C) anxious and concerned (D) spiteful and bitter
(iii) Choose the correct option : 'unmitigated burning of fossil fuels' reflects the ______ (avaricious / furious) streak in man's nature.
(iv) What message is the author giving to mankind in the extract?
questions.solution: (i) Humans compete with other species for limited resources, destroying their habitats. (ii) (C). (iii) avaricious. (iv) We must control population growth and the burning of fossil fuels and act responsibly to check global warming before it causes irreversible damage to the planet.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
The next day both men got up in good season. The crofter was in a hurry to milk his cow, and the other man probably thought he should not stay in bed when the head of the house had gotten up. They left the cottage at the same time. The crofter locked the door and put the key in his pocket. The man with the rattraps said good bye and thank you, and thereupon each went his own way.
But half an hour later the rattrap peddler stood again before the door. He did not try to get in, however. He only went up to the window, smashed a pane, stuck in his hand, and got hold of the pouch with the thirty kronor. He took the money and thrust it into his own pocket. Then he hung the leather pouch very carefully back in its place and went away. (The Rattrap)

(i) The behaviour of the peddler is an act of ______. (deceit / obedience)
(ii) 'Both men got up in good season.' 'Good season' denotes that (A) they slept for a long time (B) they got up in a good mood (C) they got up early and timely (D) they got up hurriedly
(iii) State the irony in the peddler's response, 'The man with the rattraps said good bye and thank you.'
(iv) The flaw in the peddler's character reflected in the extract is (A) he is jealous of rich people (B) he indulges in self-pity (C) he can rob his benefactor (D) he can sleep anywhere without hesitation
(v) Complete : The role of the cow in the crofter's life is ______.
(vi) Choose one instance from the extract to show that the peddler acted like a well-mannered person.
questions.solution: (i) deceit. (ii) (C). (iii) He politely thanks the crofter for his hospitality but soon returns to steal his money, betraying the man he thanked. (iv) (C). (v) that of his livelihood and companion; her milk was his source of income. (vi) He said good bye and thank you before leaving (or: he hung the pouch carefully back in its place).

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions :
'It takes longer to build a school.' I say, embarrassed at having made a promise that was not meant. But promises like mine abound in every corner of his bleak world.
After months of knowing him, I ask him his name. 'Saheb-e-Alam', he announces. He does not know what it means. If he knew its meaning – lord of the universe – he would have a hard time believing it. Unaware of what his name represents, he roams the streets with his friends, an army of barefoot boys who appear like the morning birds and disappear at noon. Over the months, I have come to recognise each of them.
'Why aren't you wearing chappals?' I ask one.
'My mother did not bring them down from the shelf.' He answers simply.
'Even if she did he will throw them off,' adds another who is wearing shoes that do not match. (Lost Spring)

(i) The intention of the speaker in the first line is one of ______. (clarification / confusion)
(ii) What is implied by 'he would have a hard time believing it'? (A) Saheb is too innocent to believe everything (B) Saheb is living up to his name (C) Saheb's living condition is contrary to the meaning of his name (D) Saheb is not used to anyone calling his name
(iii) 'Promises like mine abound in every corner of his bleak world.' People like Saheb are ______ (deluded / empowered) by such promises.
(iv) State one reason why the boy was wearing shoes that did not match.
(v) The speaker describes Saheb's life as a 'bleak world' because (A) he lives in a house without electricity (B) his world is his friends (C) his life is devoid of hope (D) he belongs to the world of illiterates
(vi) 'Why aren't you wearing chappals?' The conversation between the speaker and the boys reflects the ______ of the speaker.
questions.solution: (i) clarification. (ii) (C). (iii) deluded. (iv) He is too poor to buy a matching pair; he wears whatever discarded shoes he finds (picked up from the garbage). (v) (C). (vi) concern (curiosity and empathy) for the children.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: What valid reason does Rudyard Kipling have to call an interview immoral? (40-50 words)
questions.solution: Kipling considered an interview an assault and a crime against a person's privacy, deserving punishment; it intrudes into one's personal life, so he refused to be interviewed.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: How was self-reliance intertwined with the Champaran incident? (40-50 words)
questions.solution: Gandhi refused C.F. Andrews' help because he wanted the peasants to rely on themselves and not on an Englishman; the Champaran episode taught the sharecroppers courage, self-reliance and freedom from fear.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: 'I've plenty of time. I'll learn it tomorrow. And now you see where we've come out.' What does M. Hamel mean to convey through these lines? (40-50 words)
questions.solution: He means that the habit of putting off learning till tomorrow is the people of Alsace's great misfortune; because of this procrastination they never learnt their own language and now have lost the chance to do so.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: How can Earth play the role of a teacher according to Pablo Neruda? (40-50 words)
questions.solution: The Earth seems dead in winter but comes alive again in spring; this teaches us that apparent stillness is not death and that periods of quiet can lead to renewal and new life.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: 'And such too is the grandeur of dooms.' How can the 'grandeur of dooms' be impressive and inspiring according to Keats? (40-50 words)
questions.solution: The glorious deeds and sacrifices of great people who died for noble causes, and the honour they received, inspire us and give us hope; their memory is a thing of beauty.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: 'Christ, Sophie, you're still at school.' What image do you form of Geoff as a brother from this context? (40-50 words)
questions.solution: Geoff is a practical, realistic and somewhat dismissive older brother who brings Sophie down to earth; yet he is also affectionate and indulgent, listening to her dreams.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: Charlie's desperate attempt to find the third level reflects his frustration with the modern world. Substantiate with evidence from the story. (40-50 words)
questions.solution: Charlie says the modern world is full of insecurity, fear, war and worry; the third level, leading to Galesburg of 1894 with its peace, big shady trees and leisurely life, is his escape from the stress of the present.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.chapter: Vistas: Journey to the End of the Earth
questions.text: 'Students on Ice Programme' proves Geoff Green's farsightedness. Explain with reference to the text. (40-50 words)
questions.solution: Green takes high-school students to Antarctica because they are future policy makers; seeing the effects of climate change first-hand at an impressionable age will make them value the planet and act to protect it.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.chapter: Vistas: On the Face of It
questions.text: 'You speak peculiar things.' Why does Derry find Mr. Lamb's conversation peculiar? (40-50 words)
questions.solution: Mr. Lamb speaks optimistically about his tin leg, weeds being as beautiful as flowers, and his open gate and welcoming people despite his disability; Derry, bitter about his burnt face, finds this positive outlook strange.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.chapter: Flamingo: The Rattrap / Poets and Pancakes
questions.text: How do the peddler from 'The Rattrap' and 'the office boy' from 'Poets and Pancakes' compare in terms of their frustration, status and grudges against others? (120-150 words)
questions.solution: Value points: both are at the bottom of society and frustrated. The peddler is a poor vagabond selling rattraps and begging; he sees the world as a rattrap and resents a society that offers bait and then traps people. The office boy at Gemini Studios was a frustrated poet with literary ambitions who was stuck applying make-up; he resented Subbu and others whose success he felt was undeserved, and vented his anger on the author. Both feel unrecognised and bitter, but the peddler is redeemed by Edla's kindness, while the office boy's bitterness remains.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: Analyse the characters of William Douglas from 'Deep Water' and Mukesh from 'Lost Spring' in terms of their determination and will power in pursuing their goals. (120-150 words)
questions.solution: Value points: Douglas developed a terror of water after a childhood experience and a near-drowning at the YMCA pool; with a fixed resolve he hired an instructor, practised for months and tested himself in lakes until he conquered his fear completely, learning that 'all we have to fear is fear itself'. Mukesh, born into a family of bangle makers in Firozabad trapped by poverty, tradition and exploitation, dares to dream of becoming a motor mechanic and is determined to break the cycle. Both show courage and will power to overcome obstacles, one physical and psychological, the other social.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: Why did Dr. Sadao treat the American soldier, even though it was an unpatriotic act? Describe the difficulties faced by Dr. Sadao when he decided to help the enemy soldier. (120-150 words)
questions.solution: Value points: as a surgeon his professional ethics and humanity made him save a wounded, dying man, whoever he was. Difficulties: risk of arrest for sheltering an enemy; his servants left the house in protest; his wife Hana had to wash and nurse the soldier herself; he had to operate at home without help; when the General's assassins did not come, he arranged the soldier's escape by boat with food and clothes, keeping the secret. He balanced loyalty to his country with his duty as a doctor.

questions.subject: English Core
questions.text: 'If you want to test a man's character, give him power.' Analyse the theme of 'The Tiger King' in the light of this quote. (120-150 words)
questions.solution: Value points: the Maharaja of Pratibandapuram used his power arrogantly and whimsically; to defy the astrologer's prediction he banned tiger hunting for others and killed tigers indiscriminately, even marrying a princess of a state with many tigers. He threatened officials and exploited his subjects. His pride and abuse of power for selfish ends led to ecological damage and, ironically, his own death from a tiny wooden tiger. The story satirises the arrogance of those in power and shows that power reveals a person's true character.
